subject: Transfer Impact Appendix (TIA) template for sales & legal
messages:
From: jonas_weber@redwood.com
To: jordan_blake@redwood.com, marissa_cole@redwood.com, kimberly_park@redwood.com, laura_bennett@redwood.com
Date: Wed, 09 Dec 2026 15:12:00 -0800
Subject: Draft: Transfer Impact Appendix (TIA) template for sales & legal

Team —

I've pulled together a short, fillable Transfer Impact Appendix (TIA) template that the sales team can use during discovery with EU customers to capture the minimal set of information our privacy/legal teams need to scope SCCs/UK IDTA questions and speed up DPA signoff. The goal is to reduce back-and-forth and avoid ad-hoc addenda.

High-level: please review the attached draft and the proposed "sales checklist" section (bottom of doc). Key asks:
- Can the sales team (Jordan) confirm this captures the deal-level items you typically surface?
- Marissa / Kimberly: are the risk indicators and fallback language acceptable for initial customer-facing drafts?
- Laura: any compliance items missing for TIAs used across EU/UK + Switzerland?

Attachments: TIA_template_draft.docx (drive link included below).
Drive: https://drive.google.com/open?id=1TIAtemplate
HubSpot context: https://app.hubspot.com/deal/12345/ZENT-4231 (example)

I propose we iterate quickly and then roll the template into the sales playbook and HubSpot deal stage checklist. If legal approves, I can circulate a one-page cheat sheet for reps.

Thanks,
Jonas
Jonas Weber
Director, Privacy & Compliance
Redwood Inference

From: jordan_blake@redwood.com
To: jonas_weber@redwood.com
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.com, kimberly_park@redwood.com
Date: Thu, 10 Dec 2026 09:08:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Draft: Transfer Impact Appendix (TIA) template for sales & legal

On Wed, Dec 9, 2026 at 3:12 PM Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.com> wrote:
> Team —
> 
> I've pulled together a short, fillable Transfer Impact Appendix (TIA) template...

Thanks for pulling this together — nice work. A couple practical notes from the field:

- Reps need the template to be 1 page (max). Customers tune out multi-page legal forms during discovery. Can we move the heavy legal talk into an internal-only annex and keep the customer-facing portion a single-sheet summary?
- Please add a short checkbox for "Is on-prem or VPC required?" — that triggers an ops handoff and impacts timelines.
- Also recommend adding a simple "expected go-live window" field (0-3 / 4-8 / 9+ weeks) — we use that on every HubSpot call.

Quick question: for Zendron (ZENT-4231), Marta asked for early sight of any UK addendum language. If we include a short line that says "UK addendum expected: yes/no" that will help me avoid a second discovery call.

If you want, I can put the one-sheet into a slides template so reps can share it quickly during discovery.

-Jordan
Jordan Blake
Senior Account Executive
Redwood Inference

From: kimberly_park@redwood.com
To: jonas_weber@redwood.com, jordan_blake@redwood.com
Cc: laura_bennett@redwood.com, marissa_cole@redwood.com
Date: Thu, 10 Dec 2026 14:26:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Draft: Transfer Impact Appendix (TIA) template for sales & legal

On Thu, Dec 10, 2026 at 9:08 AM Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.com> wrote:
> Thanks for pulling this together — nice work. A couple practical notes from the field:

Jonas / team — reviewed the draft and Jordan's feedback. High-level legal steer:

1) Customer-facing one-pager: agree. Keep customer-facing section limited to factual items (processing locations, on-prem/VPC, categories of data, retention band, expected volumes). Move legal fallback language to internal annex.

2) Suggested risk indicators (for internal use only): cross-border routing yes/no; access by subprocessors outside EU/UK; high-risk categories (health, identity, financial). Those should be checkboxes in the internal annex only.

3) UK addendum: for customers that indicate UK processing or UK-based controllers/processors, include checkbox "UK addendum likely" and require early routing to Legal for a fast-track UK addendum worksheet.

4) Negotiation language: propose the following fallback phrasing for TIA summaries given most customers are not going to accept extensive technical covenants during early sales: "We will provide reasonable technical and organizational measures consistent with our DPA. Specific routing and export restrictions may require an execution of an addendum (e.g., UK IDTA) or specific contractual safeguards." (Please review — this is intentionally high-level, internal annex holds specifics.)

I've attached a redline of the draft and a short checklist that legal can sign off on.
[Attachment: Zentron_DPA_comments.pdf]

-Kim
Kimberly Park
Head of Privacy Counsel
Redwood Inference

From: laura_bennett@redwood.com
To: jonas_weber@redwood.com, kimberly_park@redwood.com, jordan_blake@redwood.com
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.com
Date: Fri, 11 Dec 2026 11:43:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Draft: Transfer Impact Appendix (TIA) template for sales & legal

For EU/UK/CH coverage — minor additions:

- Add a field "Regulated dataset (Y/N)" with examples (health, biometric, financial). If Y, require a separate feasibility check with Security and Product (include link to intake form).
- Data retention: include bands (30/90/180/indefinite) rather than free-text so we can programmatically tag deals in HubSpot.
- Subprocessor disclosures: add checkbox "Customer requires subprocessors list" + a quick path to request current subprocessor map (link) — that will cut down on ad hoc emails.

Also: for UK addendum discussions, recommend a brief internal SLA: Legal to respond within 3 business days to a UK-addendum-flagged TIA for initial eligibility. If Legal can't meet that, Sales should escalate to Jonas.

I'll update the compliance checklist and push a version to the drive.

-Laura
Laura Bennett
Senior Privacy Engineer
Redwood Inference

From: jonas_weber@redwood.com
To: jordan_blake@redwood.com, kimberly_park@redwood.com, laura_bennett@redwood.com, marissa_cole@redwood.com
Date: Sat, 12 Dec 2026 10:04:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Draft: Transfer Impact Appendix (TIA) template for sales & legal — final steps

Thanks everyone — great feedback. Plan and next steps: 

1) I'll produce a one-page customer-facing TIA summary + internal annex (legal redlines included).
2) Jordan: please confirm you want the one-sheet as a slide or a PDF for customer share — I'll produce both.
3) Kim & Laura: I'll incorporate the recommended checkboxes (UK addendum flag, on-prem/VPC, regulated dataset) and the 3-business-day SLA for UK-addendum triage.
4) Marissa: once I push the updated draft I will ask for a quick sign-off and then we will add the cheat-sheet to the sales playbook and the HubSpot deal stage checklist.

I'm going to attach the redlined draft and will circulate a final v1 on Monday. If everyone is OK, I'll also proactively send a preview to Zentron (Marta) so they can confirm the fields they need before the formal DPA. That will likely reduce follow-up cycles on ZENT-4231.

Attachments: TIA_template_draft.docx (updated will follow), Zentron_DPA_comments.pdf
